faq.title: Frequently asked questions about hospital supplementary insurance
faq.subtitle: Everything about the SDK hospital plans and the IKK classic bonus.

items.q: How much does hospital supplementary insurance cost?
items.a: The premium depends on age and plan. Current examples for a 30-year-old: Klinik bei Unfall (SPU) EUR 7.00, Klinik 2-Bett (SP2) EUR 33.41 and Klinik 1-Bett (SP1) EUR 50.72 per month. The plan calculator shows your personal premium in 2 minutes.

items.q: What is the difference between Klinik 1-Bett and Klinik 2-Bett?
items.a: Klinik 1-Bett (SP1) offers accommodation in a private or twin room and a hospital daily allowance of 10 € per day. Klinik 2-Bett (SP2) offers the twin room and an upgrade option to the private-room plan from your 30th birthday, every 5 years until age 65. Both plans include chief physician treatment without GOÄ cap, free hospital choice and rooming-in.

items.q: What is the Klinik bei Unfall plan?
items.a: SPU provides the Klinik 1-Bett benefits – private or twin room, private-doctor treatment and free hospital choice – exclusively for accident-related treatment. It requires no health assessment and costs an illustrative EUR 7.00 per month for a 30-year-old.

No. SDK waives waiting periods in its hospital plans, full cover applies from the policy start date. The only requirement: the contract must be in place before treatment, as insured events that occurred before the start date are not covered.

items.q: Are private medical fees above the maximum rate reimbursed?
items.a: Yes. Reimbursement is not capped at the maximum rates of the German medical fee schedule (GOÄ). Fees beyond that are also reimbursed, a decisive point when choosing specialists.

items.q: How does the IKK classic bonus help with financing?
items.a: For recognised activities, IKK classic gives you a choice between a cash bonus and a three-times-higher subsidy for documented eligible costs. Depending on your activities, the subsidy can cover a large part of the premium and, for the accident plan, even up to 100%. The calculator on this page shows your result.

items.q: Does the cover also apply to children?
items.a: Yes, the hospital plans are available to everyone with statutory health insurance, including children. Rooming-in is part of the benefits: one parent stays with the child in hospital.

Yes, as is usual for hospital plans, the application includes health questions. That is why the best time to sign up is while you are healthy and active. You see the questions transparently in the online application.

items.q: Who benefits most from hospital supplementary insurance?
items.a: Everyone who wants freedom of choice when it matters: athletes and active people (also via the affordable accident plan), self-employed people who need to get back on their feet quickly, and families who want to stay with their child. The requirement is statutory health insurance.

family.title: Expecting parents and children: three clear answers.
family.subtitle: If there is little time left before the birth, SDK still covers your child. If you plan early, die Bayerische costs adults less. And for children, it depends on whether illness should be covered too.

parents.label: Expecting parents · SDK
parents.title: No lead time needed
parents.body: If one parent has SDK hospital cover on the day of birth, SDK accepts your child without a health assessment, surcharge or benefit exclusion, including birth injuries and congenital conditions. There is no prior insurance period.
items: It is enough if one of you has SDK hospital cover
Your registration must reach SDK no later than two months after the birth; cover then applies from the day of birth
For a later birth: attending midwife in SP1 and SP2, family room in SP1, no waiting period
parents.note: If the pregnancy was already medically confirmed when the application was made, the plan pays neither for that birth nor for complications during it. Through newborn enrolment, your child can be insured at most as fully as the better insured parent; for SP1 this way, one parent needs SP1.

bayerische.label: Expecting parents · Bayerische
bayerische.title: Cheaper with lead time
bayerische.body: If you plan early, die Bayerische costs adults considerably less. It accepts your child without a health assessment if one parent has already been insured with die Bayerische for at least three months on the day of birth. In Komfort and Prestige, the birth itself is covered after an eight-month waiting period from the start of cover.
items: Prestige for you: EUR 13.40 a month at 21 to 30, EUR 17.60 at 31 to 45 (as of 09/2026)
For your child in the age group up to 15: Komfort EUR 3.20, Prestige EUR 4.10 a month
Family room at a later birth: in Prestige without a limit, in Komfort up to the cost of a twin room, through the mother's policy
Registration no later than two months after birth, cover backdated
If your child under 16 has to go into hospital, their Komfort or Prestige plan pays 100 per cent of your accommodation and meals as an accompanying parent, where your health insurer does not
For a later pregnancy: midwife costs beyond what your health insurer pays, in Komfort and Prestige
bayerische.note: If you are already pregnant when you apply, the plan pays neither for that birth nor for midwife costs in that pregnancy. Later on too: if a child is born before the eight months have passed, including a premature birth, the plan does not pay for the birth. Through newborn enrolment, your child can be insured at most as fully as the parent.

children.label: For children · SDK
children.title: Illness cover or accidents only?
children.body: For children, too, the cause matters: SP1 and SP2 cover agreed hospital services for illness and accidents, while SPU only applies after an accident.
items: SPU: affordable accident cover without a health assessment
children.note: SPU is not general hospital cover for children. It does not pay for inpatient treatment caused by illness.

midwife.title: Your midwife: who pays for what?
midwife.lead: Most midwife care is paid by your statutory health insurer. Here you can see what the hospital plans from SDK and die Bayerische add on top. Attending midwives (Beleghebammen) work freelance in the delivery room. You can also choose your own attending midwife, who then accompanies you to the birth in hospital.

rows.text: Antenatal care, help during the birth, home visits after the birth and the postnatal recovery course are part of the midwife care paid by statutory health insurance.
If you give birth in hospital with an attending midwife, SP1 and SP2 pay 100 per cent of the services she is entitled to bill separately. There is no waiting period.
rows.condition: This does not apply if the pregnancy was already medically confirmed when you applied. And your health insurer must cover the hospital birth.

rows.text: Home births, birth centres and care at home before and after the birth are not paid by SP1 and SP2. Your health insurer pays the midwife care for these.
According to die Bayerische's product documents, Komfort and Prestige reimburse midwife costs that go beyond what your statutory health insurer pays, including for midwives who bill privately.
rows.condition: If you are already pregnant when you apply, this does not apply to that pregnancy and birth. Die Bayerische has no general waiting period; eight months apply to childbirth.

faq.title: The key questions before you choose

items.q: What is the difference between SP1, SP2 and SPU?
items.a: SP1 offers a private or twin room and covers the statutory co-payment of EUR 10 per hospital day, paying a EUR 10 daily allowance on days without a co-payment. SP2 covers a twin room. Both apply within the agreed scope for illness and accidents. SPU covers hospital extras only after an accident.

items.q: Is SPU full hospital supplementary insurance?
items.a: SPU provides extensive hospital extras, but only for accident-related treatment. It does not pay for hospital stays caused by illness. In return, the plan requires no health assessment.

The SDK hospital plans have no policy waiting periods. Cover applies to new insured events from the start date. An insured event that occurred before then is not covered. Die Bayerische has no general waiting period; eight months apply to childbirth and psychotherapy, and these fall away after an accident.

items.q: Do I need to answer health questions?
items.a: The SP1 and SP2 applications include health questions. SPU requires no health assessment, but only pays after an accident. Binding acceptance takes place in the application.

items.q: How do I take out hospital cover?
items.a: Choose SP2, SP1 or SPU above and open the SDK premium calculator in a new tab (German form). There you enter the start date, your date of birth and gender, choose the same plan and see your premium. Your application details follow, with health questions for SP1 and SP2, and then a summary. You do not need an appointment.

items.q: Can a health fund bonus offset the entire premium?
items.a: With the affordable SPU, yes: an active health fund bonus can offset the full SPU annual premium. With SP1 and SP2 it usually offsets part of the premium, depending on your activities. It pays out at most up to your documented premium and only after the bonus year. Your personal amount depends on your health insurer, activities, proof and bonus terms.

If one parent is insured with SDK on the day of birth, register your child within two months. Cover then applies backdated to the day of birth, without a health assessment and without a prior insurance period, at most to the extent of the parent's cover. With die Bayerische, one parent must have been insured with it for at least three months on the day of birth.
